newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares end off highs, Akzo Nobel sparkles.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares end off highs, Akzo Nobel sparkles.

text.p: Dutch shares closed back from mid-afternoon highs, but posted sharp gains after the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision not to raise interest rates.
Certain stocks also provided extra impetus for the Dutch market, notably chemicals company Akzo Nobel, electronics giant Philips, the financials and brewer Heineken.
The AEX index ended up 6.64 points at 570.61.

Individually, Akzo Nobel was one of the market leaders, gaining 5.20 guilders to 204.10. The company announced that its Oganon Teknika unit had signed an agreement with China's Health Ministry to work closely on health technology research.
The company's claim at the start of the week that its new antidepressant drug Remeron was better than Ely Lilly's market leading Prozac also continued to push up the stock price.
"Admittedly, it's all longer term news, but there's no questioning its all positive," one trader said.
Philips was up 2.10 guilders at 62.70 as the semi-conductor sector in general received a boost.
The news of a lack of U.S. rate hike, at least for the time being, had a positive effect on financials. ABN AMRO was up 1.30 guilders to 93.20, while ING Bank rose 80 cents to 53.00.

However, Heineken's sharp gains confounded many traders and analysts. The stock rose 7.50 guilders to 316.00. Some said the sudden gains may have been related to the recent issue of in-the-money call warrants on Monday. Others simply said the stock had been oversold and was due to rebound.
"It's been a dog ever since its profits warning. It was bound to come back at some point," one trader said.
